reasons: No tests are visible for these shared pieces.
The logo sends company website hosts to an outside service, which the owner may want to approve or change.

terms.meaning: The small icon a website shows in a browser tab, which can be fetched as a picture of that site's identity.
A reusable piece of the screen, such as a box or a button, that the app can place wherever it is needed.
The values a parent hands to a component when it draws it.
Grey shapes shown while data is still loading, so the page does not look empty.
A button that asks the app to try loading the data again after a failure.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for shared pieces
sections.what: Brings in the state tool, the icons, and the website host helper used by the logo.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are the tools the shared pieces need.

sections.name: Panel
sections.title: Framed box with title and action
sections.what: Draws a white bordered box with an optional small label above, a bold title, an optional button or link at the top right, and a content area.
sections.why: Likely reason: every section on the portfolio pages keeps the same frame.

sections.name: Kpi
sections.title: Headline number tile
sections.what: Shows a small label above a large number, with an optional note below and a thin red bar down the left edge.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes the key figures stand out on the summary page.
sections.watch_out: The value can be text such as Not reported, and it is shown at the same large size as numbers.

sections.name: LoadingState
sections.title: Loading placeholder shapes
sections.what: Shows grey pulsing blocks in roughly the same layout as the summary page, so the page does not jump when real data arrives.
sections.why: Likely reason: matching the final layout avoids a jump when content appears.
sections.watch_out: The shapes are fixed, so a page with a different layout will look mismatched while loading.

sections.name: ErrorState
sections.title: Error box with retry button
sections.what: Shows a red-tinted box saying the portfolio data could not be loaded, displays the error message, and offers a Retry button that calls the given function.
sections.why: Reason for the exact wording is not stated. The box gives users a way to recover without reloading the whole app.
sections.watch_out: The raw error text is shown to users, which may expose technical detail.

sections.name: EmptyState
sections.title: Message when nothing matches
sections.what: Shows a dashed box with a search icon, a short title, an optional explanation and an optional action button.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It explains an empty result instead of leaving blank space.

sections.name: initials
sections.title: Two-letter name fallback
sections.what: Builds up to two capital letters from the first letters of the first two words of a name, ignoring punctuation. A name with no letters becomes a question mark.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives each company a recognizable tile when no logo image exists.
sections.watch_out: Two companies with similar names can get the same two letters, so the letters alone do not identify a company.

sections.name: CompanyLogo
sections.title: Company logo with fallback
sections.what: Shows the favicon of the company's recorded website when there is one and it loads. Otherwise shows the initials in a dashed box. An image that loads at 16 pixels or smaller is treated as a failure.
sections.why: The code comment says the logo comes only from the recorded website, with no guessed domains.
sections.watch_out: The fallback check depends on the image size, so if the outside service changes its image size, real logos may be hidden.

sections.name: Seg
sections.title: Row of toggle buttons
sections.what: Draws a row of small buttons where the current choice is highlighted, and calls the change function with the chosen value when one is clicked.
sections.why: Likely reason: a compact switch for choices such as milestone or metric.
sections.watch_out: Each button's test label is built from the group's label plus the option value, so renaming a value breaks any test that looks for the old label.

summary: Small reusable building blocks (framed boxes, headline tiles, loading placeholders, error and empty messages, company logos and toggle buttons) used across the portfolio views.
purpose: Keeps the look and the standard messages the same in every portfolio view.
why: Likely reason: sharing these pieces avoids repeating the same markup in each view. The code comment states that company logos come only from recorded websites, with no guessed domains.
how: Each piece is a small function. Panel draws a framed box with an optional label, title and action. Kpi draws a headline number. LoadingState draws pulsing placeholders. ErrorState draws a red box with a retry button. EmptyState draws a dashed message box. CompanyLogo shows the site icon of the company's recorded website, or initials when that is not possible. Seg draws a row of toggle buttons.
inputs: Titles, labels, values, notes, error objects, retry and change callbacks, and company names and websites from the views that use them.
outputs: Visual boxes, tiles, messages and buttons. The retry callback runs when Retry is pressed. The logo causes an image request to an outside favicon service.
risks: CompanyLogo sends each company's website host to Google's favicon service whenever a logo loads. That tells the outside service which company sites are being viewed, which may need an owner decision. ErrorState shows the raw error message to users, which may include technical detail.
debug: If a logo is missing, check the website value and whether the favicon service returns an image larger than 16 pixels. If an error box shows odd text, the raw error message is the source. If spacing or sizes look wrong, check the size and class values passed in by the view.
